recreation_brief:
1. Create a new PowerPoint slide with light gray background (#f0f0f0).
2. Add title text 'Derivatives of some Activation Functions' at top-left/center, bold sans-serif, dark red (#c00000), approximately 28-32pt.
3. Insert a yellow circle (#ffd700) at top-right containing the number '22' in black.
4. Draw a large white rectangle with a blue border (#0000cc) covering most of the slide area below the title.
5. Create four horizontal rows inside the rectangle. For each row:
   a. Left: Insert a rounded rectangle with light yellow fill (#ffffe0) and red border (#c00000). Type the activation function definition exactly as transcribed. Color the function name (Rectified/Parametric/Exponential/SoftPlus) red. Color 'for x≥0' green (#008000). Keep other text black.
   b. Center: Add red text 'Derivative' followed by a red double arrow '⇒'.
   c. Right: Insert a rounded rectangle with light yellow fill (#ffffe0) and blue border (#0000cc). Type the derivative formula exactly as transcribed. Color 'for x≥0' green where present.
6. Row 2 left box should end with a '+' symbol outside the closing brace.
7. Row 4 right box should display the derivative as a vertical fraction: 1 over (1 + e^(-x)).
8. Add a thin black footer bar at the very bottom of the slide.
9. Ensure all text is sans-serif and alignment matches the original (left-aligned within boxes, centered vertically in rows).
